info.title: Slotlock
info.description: Calendars agents cannot double-book. The "Agent tools" operations are the Slotlock MCP tools; the "Application" operations (resources, bookable hours, holds, reservations, coverage and maintenance) need an API key with the admin scope. An error is RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`) whose `code` names it, also as `{"error":{"code":…}}`; an overlap names the `resource_id`, `start` and `end` it refused. A write that waits for a person answers 428 `confirmation_required`.

get.description: List resources visible to the authenticated tenant principal, with what each says about itself: its name (show it rather than the reference), description, kind, capacity and labels, where it is (location), the groups it is in (a team, a department), and the pool it belongs to (a vehicle class, a room type). With kind, only resources of that kind; with labels, only those with every label given; with location, only those there or at a location in it; with group, only that group's. With pool, only that pool's members, in the order slotlock_book_pool tries them.

post.description: Create the resource with this external reference, or update its time zone, and the profile fields and location given, if the tenant already has it. Without a time zone, a new resource takes the nearest one its location, or a location above it, has, else UTC; a location the tenant does not have answers 404 location_not_found. Repeating the call changes nothing more. visibility is shared (the default: agents list and book it) or private (agents never see it), fixed at creation: naming another for an existing resource answers 409 resource_visibility_conflict. Its profile is optional: a name agents and people see instead of the reference, a description, its kind (person, room, desk, space, vehicle, machine, equipment, service or other: a hint, never a rule), its capacity (informational), up to 20 labels to find it by, and attributes you want back.

get.description: When each resource is busy in a window, as busy intervals only (never whose or what), and whether that is certain (coverage: "uncertain" where a calendar feeding it has not been read lately). Name the resources with resource_ids, or select them instead by location (and every location in it), group, labels (every one), kind or pool: at most 100 (more answers selection_too_large, none selection_empty), named in selected_resource_ids.

Find the earliest certain interval that satisfies the requested duration (up to the 367-day search window, so a multi-month rental slot can be found). Name the resources with resource_ids, or select them as slotlock_get_free_busy does: at most 100.

List up to `limit` certain slots of the requested duration, earliest first across the resources, each one free of busy time and inside the resource's hours, to offer a person a choice. With require_free, only times when at least that many of the resources are free together, each slot naming them in resource_ids: every resource for a booking that needs them all (book it with slotlock_book_together), or any n of them. No slot is listed unless every resource's coverage is certain. Name the resources with resource_ids, or select them as slotlock_get_free_busy does: at most 20.

Find hires across days, such as a car from Friday to Monday: for each resource named, or each member of a pool, the earliest range that starts between pickup_start and pickup_end and either lasts `days` days (ending at the same local time) or ends between return_start and return_end. Each range is free throughout with its buffers, allowed by the resource's booking rules (pick-up and return times, lengths, notice, step) and starts and ends inside its bookable hours. Up to `limit` ranges, earliest first, one per resource; none unless every resource's coverage is certain. Book one with slotlock_create_event, or a pool's with slotlock_book_pool, at its start and end.

post.description: Hold up to five candidate slots for a short time (30-900 seconds) while a person chooses, as alternatives in one group: each free one is held, the others are listed with why not. Book one by passing its hold_id to slotlock_create_event, which releases the rest; unbooked holds expire on their own. With payment_required, a hold is booked only once the system you book for records its payment (the person pays there): booking it before then answers payment_required, so send the person to pay and try again. A hold is yours alone, and you may have 20 live at once. A candidate refused for its time comes with alternatives (the earliest free times of its length). slotlock_confirm_slot books a held time.

get.description: What changed in the tenant, oldest first, as CloudEvents: holds made, confirmed, released or expired; bookings made, moved or cancelled; calendar events created, changed or cancelled; resources created, changed (rules, pool, hours), archived, restored or deleted; coverage sources recorded or deleted; webhooks added, enabled or deleted; API keys created, rotated or revoked (ids, times and states, never titles, attendees, URLs or secrets). With resource_ids, pools, locations (each with every location in it) or groups, only changes about a resource that matches one of them, as it is when the change is delivered: a change about no resource (a key, a webhook, a usage notice) is not sent.
